Ridu 0.2.1 improves project creation and makes the Go config-as-code workflow easier to discover and evaluate.

## Highlights

- Run `npm create ridu .` or `ridu new .` to create a project in the current directory. Ridu warns first, derives valid package names from the directory name, and preserves unrelated files. Existing project paths are reported before any project files are added.
- New projects include the initial migration required by the first production build, plus `migrate` and `start` scripts. Generated servers respect `PORT` when `RIDU_ADDRESS` is unset. If dependency setup or generation fails, the CLI preserves the scaffold and prints recovery commands.
- Explore Go examples for access control, hooks, computed fields, and typed blocks on the homepage, with a focused guide to evaluating Ridu alongside Payload and PocketBase.
- Improve search metadata, crawler discovery, and documentation navigation. Unknown website paths return a proper 404, and build checks verify the crawler and error-page output.
- Clarify installation, build, and migration workflows in the website and the release-matched coding-agent guidance.

## Compatibility and upgrading

This patch introduces no changes to public Go configuration, manifest or protocol formats, REST/SDK behavior, plugin or admin-plugin contracts, or database migration semantics. No database migration or maintenance window is required solely for this update. Current-directory creation is opt-in through `.`; new named target directories must still not exist.

Upgrade the Go module, project-local CLI, framework npm packages, and official plugins together to **0.2.1**, then run `ridu generate` and your application checks. For a project created by an earlier initializer that has no migration history yet, run `ridu migrate create --name initial` before the first production build. Review and apply any migration required by your own content-model changes through your usual deployment process.
